FAQs - Forest Department Recruitment 2026

Q1: What is the latest forest department recruitment 2026?

The latest notifications include Forest Guard, Forester, Range Forest Officer, and Group C forest posts released by state forest departments, PSCs, and staff selection boards. Check the table above for live vacancies and last dates, updated daily.

Q2: What is the last date to apply for forest department recruitment 2026?

The application last date varies by state and recruiting body - it is listed against each notification in the table above under "Last Date to Apply." Always confirm the exact date on the official notification before applying.

Q3: What is the qualification for forest guard recruitment 2026?

Most Forest Guard and Field Guard posts require a 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board. Higher posts like Forester or Range Forest Officer typically need 12th pass, a graduate degree, or a degree in a science/forestry-related field.

Q4: Is there any age relaxation for ex-servicemen in forest department recruitment?

Yes. Jobs for ex-servicemen in the forest department usually come with reserved vacancies and additional age relaxation - typically 3 to 5 years beyond the standard age limit - along with relaxed physical standards in many states.

Q5: How can I apply online for forest department vacancy 2026?

Visit the official website of the respective state forest department or recruitment board, register with your basic details, fill in the application form, upload the required documents, pay the fee, and submit. Full step-by-step details are in the "How to Apply" section above.

Q6: Which states have active forest guard recruitment 2026 notifications?

States including West Bengal, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh, and Tripura currently have or regularly release forest guard and forest officer vacancies. See the state-wise section above for details on each.

Q7: What is the salary for forest guard and forest officer posts in 2026?

Forest Guard salary typically ranges from ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 gross per month under Pay Level 3, while Range Forest Officer and ACF posts range from ₹50,000 to ₹95,000 depending on pay level. Full breakdown is in the salary table above.

Q8: Is there a written exam for forest guard recruitment 2026?

Yes, most states conduct a written exam covering General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, and Mathematics, followed by a Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and document verification before the final merit list is prepared.

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

  6. Pay the application fee (if any) and submit before the last date.
  7. Save or print the confirmation for future reference.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

The SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 has been released by the State Bank of India on 1st September 2026, following the declaration of the SBI PO Prelims Result on 28th August 2026. Candidates who appeared in the Probationary Officer Preliminary Examination held on 1st and 2nd August 2026 can now check their total and section-wise marks online. This page covers the direct download link, step-by-step download process, details shown on the scorecard, qualifying status, cut-off information, and the next steps before the SBI PO Mains Exam 2026.

Direct Link to Check SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

Quick Overview - SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

The SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 is a mark-sheet issued to every candidate who appeared in the Preliminary Examination, whether or not they qualified for the Mains stage. It shows the marks obtained in each section along with the total score and qualifying status. Prelims marks are used only for shortlisting candidates for the Mains exam and are not added to the final merit list.

Particulars Details
Exam Name SBI PO Preliminary Examination 2026
Conducting Body State Bank of India (SBI)
Advertisement No. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09
Post Name Probationary Officer (PO)
Total Vacancies 1,500
SBI PO Prelims Exam Date 1st and 2nd August 2026
Candidates Appeared Approximately 11 lakh
SBI PO Prelims Result Date 28th August 2026
Candidates Shortlisted for Mains 15,802
SBI PO Score Card Release Date 1st September 2026
SBI PO Mains Exam Date 2026 12th September 2026
Mode of Score Card Online

Important Dates for SBI PO Recruitment 2026

  • SBI PO Prelims Exam: 1 and 2 August 2026
  • SBI PO Prelims Result Declared: 28 August 2026
  • SBI PO Prelims Score Card Released: 1 September 2026
  • SBI PO Mains Exam: 12 September 2026
  • SBI PO Mains Admit Card: Not Available Officially

SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 Direct Link

The direct link to check the SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 is active on the official SBI recruitment portal. Candidates should use only the official link below rather than unofficial third-party websites to avoid entering their details on unsafe pages.

SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 - Official Download Link

Details Required to Check SBI PO Score Card 2026

Candidates need the following details ready before logging in to check their score card. Source reports on the exact second login field are inconsistent — some describe it as the account password, others as the date of birth. Keep both on hand to avoid a failed login attempt.

  • Registration Number or Roll Number (mandatory)
  • Password or Date of Birth, depending on the login screen displayed (see discrepancy note below)
  • Captcha / text verification code

How to Download SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

  1. Visit the official SBI website at sbi.co.in and go to the Careers section.
  2. Click on "Current Openings" and find the Probationary Officer recruitment link (CRPD/PO/2026-27/09).
  3. Click on the "SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026" or "Marks Secured by the Candidates in Preliminary Examination" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number or Roll Number.
  5. Enter your Password or Date of Birth, as prompted on screen.
  6. Enter the captcha/verification code and click Submit.
  7. Your SBI PO Prelims Score Card will appear on the screen.
  8. Check all details carefully and download or take a printout for future reference.

Details Mentioned in SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

The SBI PO Score Card 2026 displays the following details. Candidates are advised to verify every field carefully and report any discrepancy to SBI through the official channel.

Field Description
Candidate Name As per application form
Roll Number / Registration Number Unique candidate identifier
Date of Birth As per application form
Category General/EWS/OBC/SC/ST/PwBD as applicable
Post Applied For Probationary Officer
Exam Date 1 or 2 August 2026 (as applicable to the candidate's shift)
Section-Wise Marks Marks obtained in each Prelims section
Total Marks / Aggregate Score Overall score out of 100
Qualifying Status Qualified / Not Qualified for Mains

Important Instructions for SBI PO Score Card 2026

  • Use only the official SBI website or Careers portal to check and download your score card; avoid third-party links.
  • Keep your Registration Number/Roll Number, Date of Birth, and password handy before attempting to log in.
  • Cross-check the domain name in your browser address bar before entering personal details.
  • Download and save a copy of the score card for future reference, as it may be required at later stages of recruitment.
  • In case of login errors, this can occur due to incorrect details, heavy website traffic, or a temporary technical issue — wait and retry rather than repeatedly submitting incorrect information.
  • Report any factual error on your score card to SBI through the official grievance/contact channel rather than assuming it will self-correct.

SBI PO Mains Exam 2026: Next Step

Candidates shortlisted through the SBI PO Prelims Result 2026 will appear for the SBI PO Mains Examination scheduled on 12th September 2026. The Mains exam includes both an objective test and a descriptive paper, with negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applicable to the objective section only. The SBI PO Mains Admit Card release date is Not Available Officially at the time of this update. Shortlisted candidates are advised to use their Prelims score card to identify weaker sections and focus preparation accordingly on reasoning, data analysis, English language, general/economy/banking awareness, and descriptive writing.

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) has released the notification for the Common Recruitment Process for Regional Rural Banks, 15th cycle (CRP RRBs-XV), inviting online applications for Group "A" Officer (Scale-I, II & III) and Group "B" Office Assistant (Multipurpose) posts across 28 Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) in India. IBPS RRB Recruitment 2026 online registration opens on 1 September 2026 and closes on 21 September 2026.

Quick answer: IBPS is recruiting for Officer Scale-I, II (seven specialisations), III, and Office Assistant (Multipurpose) posts, with an indicative 13,706 vacancies spread across 28 RRBs covering nearly every state and union territory of India. Graduates in any discipline (with specific additional qualifications for certain Officer Scale-II specialist roles) between 18 and 40 years of age (depending on the post) can apply online only, from 1 September 2026 to 21 September 2026, at the official IBPS website, www.ibps.in.

IBPS RRB Vacancy 2026 - Post-Wise Details

IBPS has released indicative, RRB-wise and category-wise vacancies for each post in Annexure-I of the notification. The notification itself does not print a single consolidated grand-total figure; the totals below are computed by summing the individual state/RRB-wise tables for each post category. One participating bank, Tripura Gramin Bank, has reported "NR" (Not Reported) against every post, so it is excluded from these computed totals and the true final vacancy count will be higher once that figure is released.

Candidates can check the RRB-wise, category-wise (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/General) breakup for their state directly in Annexure-I of the official notification, since a state/category-level reproduction is too extensive for this summary.

IBPS RRB Eligibility Criteria & Qualification

Nationality: a candidate must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who arrived before 1 January 1962 intending to settle permanently in India, or a person of Indian origin migrated from certain specified countries with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India.

Educational qualification (as on the last date of online registration, i.e. 21.09.2026) varies by post:

Post Essential Educational Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Office Assistant (Multipurpose) Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university or equivalent; proficiency in the local language prescribed by the participating RRB; working knowledge of computers is desirable Not required
Officer Scale-I (Assistant Manager) Bachelor's degree in any discipline; preference to candidates with a degree in Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry, Veterinary Science, Agricultural Engineering, Pisciculture, Agricultural Marketing and Cooperation, IT, Management, Law, Economics or Accountancy; local language proficiency required Not required
Officer Scale-II - General Banking Officer Bachelor's degree in any discipline with minimum 50% aggregate marks; preference to specified subject backgrounds 2 years as an officer in a bank or financial institution
Officer Scale-II - Information Technology Officer Bachelor's degree in Electronics/Communication/Computer Science/IT or equivalent, minimum 50% aggregate marks 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Chartered Accountant Certified Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 1 year as a Chartered Accountant
Officer Scale-II - Law Officer Degree in Law from a recognised university, minimum 50% aggregate marks 2 years as an advocate, or as a Law Officer in a bank/financial institution
Officer Scale-II - Treasury Manager Chartered Accountant, or MBA in Finance from a recognised university/institution 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Marketing Officer MBA in Marketing from a recognised university 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Agricultural Officer Bachelor's degree in Agriculture/Horticulture/Dairy/Animal Husbandry/Forestry/Veterinary Science/Agricultural Engineering/Pisciculture, minimum 50% aggregate marks 2 years in the relevant field
Officer Scale-III (Senior Manager) Bachelor's degree in any discipline, minimum 50% aggregate marks; preference to specified subject backgrounds Minimum 5 years as an officer in a bank or financial institution

Candidates awarded CGPA/OGPA must convert it to a percentage as per their university's own conversion criteria, and the result for the qualifying degree must have been declared on or before 21.09.2026.

IBPS RRB Age Limit

Age is reckoned as on 01.09.2026.

Post Age Limit
Office Assistant (Multipurpose) 18 to 28 years
Officer Scale-I (Assistant Manager) Above 18, below 30 years
Officer Scale-II (Manager) Above 21, below 32 years
Officer Scale-III (Senior Manager) Above 21, below 40 years

Age relaxation is available as follows: 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC (non-creamy layer), 10 years for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD), and additional relaxation for Ex-Servicemen and (for Office Assistant only) widows, divorced women, and women legally separated from their husbands who have not remarried. Relaxation for SC/ST/OBC is cumulative with only one other applicable category.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

IBPS RRB Application Fee

Category Fee (Officer Scale I/II/III) Fee (Office Assistant)
SC/ST/PwBD (and ESM/DESM for Office Assistant) ₹175 (inclusive of GST) ₹175 (inclusive of GST)
All other candidates ₹850 (inclusive of GST) ₹850 (inclusive of GST)

Payment is online only, between 01.09.2026 and 21.09.2026. Bank transaction charges for online payment are to be borne by the candidate. A candidate applying for both an Officer post and the Office Assistant post must pay the fee separately for each.

Also Read: IOB Generalist/SO Recruitment 2026 - Apply Online for 291 Manager, Assistant Manager and Senior Manager Posts

IBPS RRB Salary & Exam Pattern

Salary: Not specified in the notification.

Exam pattern: The online examination structure differs by post and stage.

Post Stage Sections Total Marks Duration
Office Assistant / Officer Scale-I Preliminary Reasoning, Numerical Ability/Quantitative Aptitude 80 45 minutes
Office Assistant / Officer Scale-I Main Reasoning, Computer Knowledge, General Awareness, English/Hindi Language, Numerical Ability/Quantitative Aptitude 200 120 minutes
Officer Scale-III (Single-level exam) Single Reasoning, Computer Knowledge, Financial Awareness, English/Hindi Language, Quantitative Aptitude & Data Interpretation 200 120 minutes

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in the objective tests; unattempted questions are not penalised. Officer Scale-II candidates sit for a single-level examination (structure not itemised separately in the notification excerpt reviewed here beyond the general pattern above).

Also read: IBPS RRB Clerk Exam Pattern and Syllabus 2026: Download PDF Here

IBPS RRB Selection Process

  • Office Assistant (Multipurpose): Preliminary Exam → Main Exam → Provisional Allotment (based on Main Exam marks and actual vacancies reported by the RRB).
  • Officer Scale-I: Preliminary Exam → Main Exam → Common Interview → Provisional Allotment.
  • Officer Scale-II & III: Single-level online exam → Common Interview → Provisional Allotment.
  • Interview is out of 100 marks; minimum qualifying marks are 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates).
  • The relative weightage for Officer posts is 80% online exam and 20% interview.
  • Interviews for Officer posts are coordinated by the Nodal Regional Rural Bank with the assistance of NABARD and IBPS.

How to Apply for IBPS RRB Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official IBPS website, www.ibps.in, and open the "CRP for RRBs" link on the home page.
  2. Click "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE FOR CRP-RRBs-OFFICERS (Scale-I, II and III)" or "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE FOR CRP-RRBs-OFFICE ASSISTANTS (Multipurpose)", as applicable.
  3. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic details to generate a provisional registration number and password (also sent by SMS/email).
  4. Log back in using the provisional registration number and password to complete the rest of the form.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, a handwritten declaration, and your Class 10 (SSC/SSLC) certificate, plus any category/disability certificates applicable to you, as per the scanning specifications in Annexure-III.
  6. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online.
  7. Candidates applying for both Office Assistant and an Officer post, or reconsidering their choice of Officer scale, must register and pay separately for each post.
  8. Take a printout of the final submitted application form for future reference.

Documents Required

  • Printout of the valid interview call letter (for Officer posts)
  • System-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or Class 10/SSLC certificate showing DOB)
  • Photo identity proof
  • Mark-sheets/certificates for the qualifying degree, with proof the result was declared on or before 21.09.2026
  • Experience certificate(s), where the post requires post-qualification experience
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL, in the prescribed Government of India format), where applicable
  • Income and Asset Certificate for EWS candidates, where applicable
  • Disability certificate/UDID card, where applicable
  • Ex-servicemen documents (discharge certificate/pension payment order, or the relevant proforma), where applicable

Bank of India (BOI), a leading Public Sector Bank with its Head Office in Mumbai, has released a notification for the recruitment of Officers in various Specialist streams up to Scale IV. Under Project No. 2026-27/02 dated 01.08.2026, BOI is inviting applications for 205 vacancies across 48 distinct posts ranging from Officer (Scale I) to Chief Manager (Scale IV). Candidates with qualifications in Computer Science/IT, Law, Fire Engineering, and Civil Engineering can apply online between 10.09.2026 and 25.09.2026.

In brief: BOI is recruiting for IT and specialist officer roles spanning Full-Stack Engineering, Digital Platforms, Information Security, DevSecOps, Data Engineering, Database Administration, Law Officer, Fire Officer, Security Officer, and Civil Engineer, among others. Eligible Indian citizens (and other nationalities specified in the notice) meeting the post-specific qualification and experience criteria as on 01.08.2026 can apply online through the official BOI website. The application mode is online only, and postings will be anywhere in India.

Bank of India Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

Minimum and maximum age are calculated as on 01.08.2026 and vary by post - from 21-30 years for Scale I Officer posts up to 28-42 years for Scale IV Chief Manager posts. BOI Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Online Examination: English Language (25 marks, qualifying only) + Professional Knowledge relevant to the post (100 marks), composite duration 100 minutes
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 35% for General/EWS (30% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD)
  • Personal Interview: Maximum 100 marks; qualifying 50% for General/EWS, 45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD; candidates called at approximately 1:3 ratio to vacancies
  • Final weightage: Online Examination and Interview combined at 60:40
  • Bank may, at its discretion, select solely through Interview without an online exam

  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates in government/PSU employment)

How to Apply for Bank of India Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official website www.bankofindia.bank.in and click on 'CAREER'
  2. Click the link "Recruitment of Officers in various streams upto Scale IV – Project No. 2026-27/02 Notice dated 01.08.2026"
  3. Click 'APPLY ONLINE' and complete new registration to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password
  4. Fill in personal, educational, and experience details; upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per specifications
  5. Preview and verify all details before clicking 'COMPLETE REGISTRATION'
  6. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online
  7. Take a printout of the system-generated application form and e-receipt for personal record

Important Instructions

IOB Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility (age, educational qualification, and post-qualification work experience) is assessed as on 01.08.2026 for all posts. Candidates must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from specified countries with the intention of permanently settling in India (subject to an eligibility certificate from the Government of India for the latter categories).

Post Code Post Name Age (Min–Max) Educational Qualification Post Qualification Work Experience

Certification requirements, technology-domain specifics, and detailed sub-conditions for each Specialist Officer post are extensive; candidates are advised to refer to the full official notification PDF for the complete post-wise qualification and experience matrix before applying.

IOB Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

The minimum and maximum age for each post is listed in the eligibility table above (assessed as on 01.08.2026). Age relaxation for reserved categories is as follows:

Category Age Relaxation

Other Backward Classes (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years

Persons affected by 1984 riots 5 years
Ex-Servicemen / Commissioned Officers (min. 5 years military service) 5 years

Cumulative age relaxation across categories is available to SC/ST/OBC candidates, subject to a maximum upper age limit of 50 years. There is no reservation for Ex-servicemen in the Officers' cadre, though age relaxation applies as per Government guidelines.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

IOB Recruitment 2026 Salary

Selected candidates will be placed in the following pay scales, with DA, HRA, CCA, and other allowances as per rules in force.

Scale / Grade Scale of Pay (₹)

MMGS II 64820 – 2340/1 – 67160 – 2680/10 – 93960

Specialist Officers recruited laterally in MMG Scale II and III are also eligible for Conveyance Expenses, Newspaper Cost, Telephone/Mobile Expenses, Residential Furniture, and Bank-owned or leased accommodation during probation, as per extant Bank guidelines. Selected candidates must execute a Financial Service Indemnity Bond of ₹2,00,000 (JMGS I, minimum 3 years' service) or ₹2,50,000 (MMGS II & III, minimum 3 years' service).

IOB Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

Category Application Fee / Intimation Charges
SC / ST / PWD ₹175/- (inclusive of GST)
All Others (including OBC & EWS) ₹1,000/- (inclusive of GST)

Payment can be made online via Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or BHIM/UPI. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other recruitment process.

IOB Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Selection is through an Online Examination followed by a Personal Interview.
  • For Post Code 01 (Manager – Branch Management): the Online Examination has 100 questions/100 marks in 2 hours, covering English Language (25Q, 30 minutes) and Professional Knowledge – Banking Law & Practice, Indian Economy & Financial System, Principles & Practices of Banking, Accounting & Financial Management (75Q, 90 minutes).
  • For all other posts: the Online Examination has 100 questions/100 marks in 2 hours, covering English Language (25Q, 30 minutes), General Awareness with special reference to Banking Industry (25Q, 30 minutes), and Professional Knowledge, which varies post-wise (50Q, 60 minutes).
  • There is no minimum qualifying mark for General Awareness and English Language; candidates must secure minimum qualifying marks in Professional Knowledge.
  • Minimum qualifying marks in the Online Examination: 35% for unreserved candidates, 30% for reserved candidates.
  • 1/4th of the marks allotted to a question is deducted for a wrong answer; there is no penalty for unattempted questions.
  • The Interview carries a maximum of 100 marks, assessed on Role-related Industry Exposure, Subject Knowledge, and Communication Skills. Minimum qualifying marks: 50% for unreserved, 45% for reserved candidates.
  • The final merit list is prepared with 80% weightage to the Online Examination and 20% weightage to the Interview.

IOB Recruitment 2026 Documents Required

  • Printout of the valid Interview Call Letter
  • System-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate or Std. X Certificate with DOB)
  • Photo Identity Proof (Passport/Aadhaar/e-Aadhaar/PAN Card/Driving Licence/Voter's Card)
  • Mark sheets and certificates for educational qualifications
  • Work experience proof (Experience Certificates, Appointment Letters, Relieving Letters, Salary Slips)
  • Certificates for preferred professional certifications, where applicable
  • Caste Certificate (for SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS candidates, in the prescribed format)
  • Disability Certificate (for PWBD candidates, issued by the District Medical Board)
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates currently in Government/PSU/Bank service)

Ration Card will not be accepted as a valid ID proof at any stage of this recruitment process.

How to Apply for IOB Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official IOB website, www.iob.bank.in, and open the "Careers" page.
  2. Click on "Recruitment of Generalist/Specialist Officers in Various Scales – 2026-27" and select the post to be applied for.
  3. Click "Register Online" and complete first-time registration.
  4. Note the system-generated Registration Number and Password sent via e-mail and SMS.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and handwritten declaration as per the prescribed specifications.
  6. Fill in all required details in the online application form carefully and click "Complete Registration."
  7. Pay the applicable Application Fee / Intimation Charges online (Debit Card/Credit Card/Internet Banking/BHIM/UPI).
  8. Take a printout of the submitted application form and the payment e-receipt for future reference.

IOB Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Applications can be submitted online only, from 29.08.2026 to 15.09.2026; no other mode will be accepted.
  • Candidates may apply for more than one post, subject to fulfilling the eligibility criteria for each.
  • If a candidate submits multiple applications for the same post, only the last submitted application will be considered.
  • Incomplete applications or those without supporting documents will be rejected outright.
  • OBC candidates must submit a non-creamy layer certificate valid as on the date of interview.
  • The Bank reserves the right to change, modify, cancel, or add to any of the eligibility or selection criteria.
  • Outstation SC/ST/PWBD candidates who are unemployed will be reimbursed second-class train fare by the shortest route, as per Government guidelines.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification.
  • Requests for change of examination centre, interview date, or registered e-mail ID will not be entertained.
  • The Online Examination will be conducted at centres including Delhi/NCR, Mumbai/Navi Mumbai/MMR/Thane, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.

BOB Local Bank Officer Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must fulfil the following eligibility conditions, assessed as on the cut-off date of 01.08.2026, to apply for BOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026.

Nationality Citizen of India, or subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 with intent to permanently settle, or a person of Indian origin who migrated from specified countries (Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, Vietnam) with intent to permanently settle in India

Candidates who have resigned from an officer-grade position in Bank of Baroda, or exited the Bank while on contract within the last three years as on the cut-off date, are not eligible to apply.   1. Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at rbi.org.in and go to the "Opportunities@RBI" section, or use the direct score card login link on the official results page.
  2. Click on "Current Vacancies," then locate the RBI Assistant Recruitment 2026 (Panel Year 2025) link.
  3. Open the "Marksheet of Preliminary Examination" or "Score Card" link for the Assistant post.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number in the first field.
  5. Enter your Password (this is generally your Date of Birth, in DD-MM-YY format).
  6. Type the Captcha code exactly as shown.
  7. Click the Submit button.
  8. Your score card will be displayed on the screen download and save it, or take a printout for future reference.

RBI Assistant Prelims Cut Off 2026

The category-wise and office-wise cut off marks have been released alongside the score card. The cut off table indicates the minimum qualifying marks for General, SC, ST, OBC, EWS, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen categories, along with sectional cut off marks for each subject. Where no vacancy exists for a category at a particular office, the cut off may be shown as "-", and in some cases all qualified candidates are merit-listed rather than shortlisted against a fixed cut off.

Important Instructions

  • Verify every detail on your score card carefully, including your name, roll number, category, and marks.
  • RBI does not send score cards through email or SMS they must be downloaded manually from the official portal.
  • Compare your marks against the official category-wise cut off before assuming your qualifying status.
  • If any information on your score card appears incorrect, contact RBI through the official channels mentioned on the recruitment portal.
  • Keep a downloaded copy or printout of the score card for future reference, including for the Mains stage and beyond.
  • Start preparing for the Mains Examination immediately, focusing on sections where your sectional marks were relatively weaker.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Vacancy 2026 - Category & Unit-wise Details

Vacancies are divided into two categories - Fresher (163 posts) and Ex-ITI (4,308 posts) - spread across Carriage & Wagon Works Perambur, Central Workshop Ponmalai, Signal & Telecommunication Workshop Podanur, Railway Hospital Perambur, and multiple divisions (Chennai, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli, Palakkad, Salem, Trivandrum).

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Eligibility Criteria

Only candidates residing within the following areas (Geographical Jurisdiction of Southern Railway) are eligible to apply:

  • Whole State of Tamil Nadu
  • Whole Union Territory of Puducherry
  • Whole State of Kerala
  • Whole Union Territories of Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep Islands
  • Only two districts of Andhra Pradesh: SPSR Nellore and Chittoor
  • Only one district of Karnataka: Dakshina Kannada

Candidates must also meet the minimum standards of physical fitness under Schedule-II of the Apprenticeship Rules, 1992, verified through a medical certificate from a Government-Authorized Doctor at the time of document verification.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Qualification

Fresher Category:

  • Fitter, Painter, Welder - Passed 10th Class (minimum 50% aggregate) under the 10+2 system or equivalent.
  • Medical Laboratory Technician (Radiology/Pathology/Cardiology) - Passed 12th Class (minimum 50% aggregate) with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology.

Ex-ITI Category:

  • Most trades (Fitter, Machinist, MMV, Turner, Diesel Mechanic, Carpenter, Painter, Welder(G&E), Wireman, Advance Welder, Plumber, Draughtsman-Civil, Instrument Mechanic, Mech. R&AC, Gas Cutter, MMTM, Structural Welder) - Passed 10th Class (min. 50%) + ITI course in the relevant trade with an NCVT/SCVT certificate.
  • Electrician - Same as above, with Science as a subject in 10th.
  • Electronics Mechanic - Same as above, with Science (Physics & Chemistry) and Mathematics.
  • Secretarial Assistant & Stenographer (English) - Passed 12th Class + ITI course with NCVT/SCVT certificate.
  • ICTSM - Passed 10th Class + ITI course with NCVT/SCVT certificate.
  • COPA/PASAA - Passed 10th Class (min. 50%) + National Trade Certificate in Computer Operator and Programming Assistant.

Note: The minimum 50% requirement in 10th standard does not apply to SC/ST/PwBD candidates. Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAAs), Engineering Graduates/Diploma holders, or Vocational Certificate holders with one year or more of training/job experience after these qualifications are not eligible.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Age Limit

As on the date of notification (28-08-2026):

  • Minimum age: 15 years completed
  • Maximum age: 22 years (Fresher/Ex-ITI) / 24 years (MLT)
  • Upper age relaxation: 3 years for OBC-(NCL), 5 years for SC/ST, 10 years for PwBD
  • Combined relaxation for PwBD candidates: UR/EWS + PwBD = 10 years; OBC-(NCL) + PwBD = 13 years; SC/ST + PwBD = 15 years

To avoid any confusion regarding age eligibility, candidates can use our Age Calculator to calculate their exact age based on the prescribed cut-off date before applying.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Stipend

Category Stipend (per month)
Fresher's - 10th Std Rs. 8,200/-
Fresher's - 12th Std Rs. 9,600/-
Ex-ITI Rs. 9,600/-

Stipend increases by 10% in the second year of training and a further 15% in the third year, over the prescribed minimum.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Application Fee

Processing fee of Rs. 100/- (non-refundable), payable online. No fee is required for SC/ST/PwBD/Women candidates.

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Selection Process

Selection is based on a Merit List, prepared as follows:

  • Fresher Category: Matriculation marks converted to 200 (minimum 50% aggregate required, except SC/ST/PwBD).
  • Ex-ITI Category: Matriculation marks converted to 100 + ITI marks converted to 100 = 200 total, with equal weightage to both.
  • MLT Category: Higher Secondary marks (Physics, Chemistry, Maths & Biology) converted to 200.

In case of a tie, the older candidate is preferred; if birth dates are also the same, the candidate who passed Matriculation earlier is preferred.

How to Apply for Southern Railway Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit www.sr.indianrailways.gov.in
  2. Navigate to News & Updates → Personnel Branch Information
  3. Complete the online application in all respects before the closing date.
  4. Submit the application online between 28-08-2026 and 27-09-2026 (till 17:00 Hrs).

Southern Railway Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • This notification is purely for apprenticeship training, not employment - there is no guarantee of employment after training.
  • 20% of vacancies in Direct Recruitment to Level 1 posts may give preference to Course Completed Act Apprentices (CCAAs) holding a National Apprenticeship Certificate (NAC).
  • All official communication - notifications, document verification lists, selection and eligibility results - will be posted only on the official website link mentioned above.
  • Candidates availing SC/ST/OBC-NCL/PwBD benefits must produce the relevant certificate at document verification, else they will be treated as UR.
  • False declarations will lead to disqualification/termination at any stage without notice.
  • Candidates are responsible for arranging their own accommodation during training.
  • Ex-ITI candidates must possess the relevant ITI qualification at the time of applying.

Assistant Officer (all disciplines) 18–32 years

Age Relaxation

Category Relaxation
SC / ST 5 years
OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 3 years

Ex-servicemen (ESM) 3 years plus period of service
Departmental candidates 5 years
Note: Maximum upper age of an applicant, including all possible age relaxations, must not exceed 50 years. Age concession to PwBD candidates is admissible irrespective of whether the specific post is reserved for PwBD. Ex-servicemen already in regular Central/State Government/CPSE/Autonomous Body employment get age relaxation for another post but are not eligible for the reservation benefit.

CONCOR Recruitment 2026 Pay Scale & CTC

Post Pay Scale Approx. CTC (Per Annum)
Management Trainee (all disciplines) ₹50,000-3%-1,60,000 ₹20.11 Lakhs
Assistant Officer (all disciplines) ₹40,000-3%-1,36,000 ₹16.09 Lakhs
Management Trainees undergo one year of on-the-job and off-the-job training and, on successful completion, are absorbed in the Assistant Manager grade/E1. Selected MT candidates must execute a service bond of ₹2 Lakhs plus 12% interest per annum, to serve CONCOR for a minimum of three years (excluding the training period).

CONCOR Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Management Trainee: Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by Group Discussion and/or Interview, as decided by CONCOR. CONCOR's decision is final and binding.
  • Assistant Officer: Selection is purely based on performance in the Online Test (CBT) – there is no GD or interview stage for this post.
  • No correspondence will be entertained for non-calling of a candidate for the Online Test/GD/Interview, or for non-selection.

CBT Exam Pattern (MT & AO)

Section No. of Questions Max. Marks
Professional Knowledge 50 50
English Language 10 10
Reasoning 10 10
Quantitative Aptitude 15 15
General Knowledge 15 15
Total 100 100
  • Duration: 90 minutes total (120 minutes for eligible PwBD candidates availing a scribe).
  • Negative marking: 1/4 (0.25) mark deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Each question has 5 answer choices.
  • The question paper is set in English and Hindi only; the English version prevails in case of any discrepancy.
  • Candidates opt for 3 Test Cities in order of preference at the time of application; this cannot be changed after submission. CONCOR reserves the right to cancel or add examination centres at its discretion.

How to Apply for CONCOR Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the CONCOR website concorindia.co.in and go to 'HR & Career Section → Recruitment and Result'.
  2. Before starting, keep a valid personal e-mail ID and mobile number ready and active till the process completes – create a new e-mail ID first if you don't have one.
  3. Fill in the online application form as per the instructions provided on the portal and pay the applicable fee online.
  4. Candidates applying for more than one post must submit a separate application form with the prescribed fee for each post code.
  5. Submit the application by 30 September 2026, 11:55 PM. No other mode of application (offline/postal) is accepted.
  6. Registration number, password, e-Admit Card, Call Letter for Document Verification/GD/Interview and other communication will be sent only to the registered e-mail ID/SMS – check your spam/junk folder as well.
Important: Applications received without the prescribed fee, required documents and information are liable to be rejected. Fee once paid is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any future recruitment.

Application Fee & Documents Required

Category Fee for MT Fee for AO
General (UR) / OBC (Creamy & Non-Creamy Layer) / EWS ₹750 + GST ₹500 + GST
SC / ST / PwBD / Ex-servicemen Exempted – no fee payable

Fee is accepted online only; bank transaction/intimation charges are borne by the candidate. Documents to be produced in original at the time of document verification (for candidates who qualify the CBT) include:

  • All educational qualification certificates and mark sheets (final mark sheet/degree, if provisionally applied while in the final year/semester)
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL, in the prescribed proforma; OBC-NCL certificate not older than 1 year)
  • Disability certificate from the Competent Authority, for PwBD reservation/relaxation (40% or more disability)
  • Income and Asset Certificate, not older than 1 year, for EWS reservation
  • Defence Service Certificate from the Competent Authority, for Ex-servicemen candidates
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the current employer, for candidates already employed on a regular basis in Government/Semi-Government/PSU/Autonomous Bodies
  • A notarized English or Hindi translation, if any SC/ST/OBC-NCL/PwBD/EWS certificate is issued in another language

Important Conditions

  • CONCOR does not undertake detailed scrutiny of eligibility at the application/CBT stage – candidature is accepted only provisionally; candidates must satisfy themselves of their eligibility before applying.
  • If claims of qualification/caste/category made in the application are not substantiated by documents at verification, the candidature will be cancelled; furnishing wrong or false information, or suppressing information, leads to disqualification and, even if appointed, termination of service.
  • If the candidate's identity is in doubt, or requisite documents cannot be produced, or there is a mismatch in document information, the candidate will not be allowed to appear for Document Verification and the candidature is liable to be cancelled.
  • Selected candidates are liable to be posted at any office/terminal/unit of CONCOR at any location, at the company's sole discretion, and liable to transfer anywhere thereafter.
  • If marks in the qualifying exam are in CGPA terms, they should not be lower than 7 points on a 10-point scale, or the equivalent percentage, and not less than the prescribed percentage for the respective post.
  • Where a Management/Engineering qualification has dual specialization, one specialization must be function-specific to the post advertised.
  • Experience requirements must be in the areas specified in the post's job specification; there is no experience requirement for ex-servicemen candidates.
  • No travelling expenses are paid for the online test or Group Discussion; candidates appearing for interview get travel expense reimbursement as per CONCOR's TA/DA rules.
  • Canvassing in any form disqualifies the candidate.
  • Appointment is subject to verification of original documents (age, qualification, experience, caste), police verification, reference checks, and fitness in the Medical Fitness Test conducted by CONCOR's Medical Authorities.
  • Management has the right to cancel the recruitment at any point without notice, and the number of posts may increase or decrease at CONCOR's sole discretion.
  • In case of any ambiguity from interpretation in a version other than English, the English version prevails. Any dispute regarding this recruitment will be settled within the jurisdiction of Delhi only.

RRB Group D Application Status 2026: The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) have issued a revised notice on the application status for CEN No. 09/2025 (Level-1) recruitment. Candidates can now check their updated application status provisionally accepted, conditionally accepted, or rejected by logging in at www.rrbapply.gov.in. The revised status is being updated from August 9, 2026, at 9:00 PM (21:00 Hrs) onward.

Particulars Details
Recruitment RRB Group D (Level-1 posts)
CEN Number CEN No. 09/2025

Status Categories Provisionally Accepted, Conditionally Accepted (with conditions), Rejected (with reasons)

RRB Group D Application Status: Categories Explained

Candidates can now view their updated status under three categories:

  • Provisionally Accepted: The application has been accepted on a provisional basis. It is not a final confirmation, and RRB can still cancel the candidature at any later stage if any discrepancy is found.
  • Conditionally Accepted: The application has been accepted subject to certain conditions. Candidates must check the specific conditions mentioned against their application and follow RRB's instructions.
  • Rejected: The application has been rejected, and the reason for rejection will be shown along with the status.

Also Read: RRB Group D Admit Card 2026

How to Check RRB Group D Application Status 2026

  1. Visit the official RRB application portal: www.rrbapply.gov.in.
  2. Log in using your registered user credentials.
  3. Navigate to the application status section for CEN No. 09/2025.
  4. View your status: Provisionally Accepted, Conditionally Accepted, or Rejected.
  5. If rejected, check the reason for rejection displayed against your application.
  6. Save or take a screenshot of the status page for future reference.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • The list of provisionally eligible candidates has been prepared carefully, but RRB reserves the right to rectify any inadvertent error or typographical/printing mistake.
  • RRB will not entertain any correspondence from ineligible or rejected candidates.
  • Candidature of all eligible/accepted candidates is purely provisional and can be cancelled at any stage of the recruitment process or even afterward if any inconsistency, deficiency, falsified record, or malpractice is found.
  • Candidates should refer only to official RRB websites for recruitment updates and must not rely on unauthenticated sources.
  • RRB has warned candidates to stay alert against touts who make false promises of selection in exchange for illegal consideration. The RRB recruitment process is fully computerized, and selection is based purely on merit.

Also Read: RRB Group D City Intimation Slip 2026

What to Do After Checking Your Status

If your application shows as provisionally or conditionally accepted, continue preparing for the next stage of the CEN 09/2025 recruitment process as and when RRB announces it. If your application is rejected, review the stated reason; RRB has clarified that it will not respond to correspondence from rejected candidates on this matter.

This article covers the download link, objection process, important dates, and answers to the questions candidates are asking most.

KEA Kannada Language Test 2026 What It Is

The Compulsory Kannada Language Test is a qualifying test, not a merit-ranking exam. It applies only to candidates from the outside-Karnataka and Kalyana-Karnataka quota who have not studied or passed their qualifying examination in Kannada, or who have not cleared an equivalent Kannada test, or who have not completed SSLC-level schooling with Kannada as a first or second language. Clearing this test alone does not guarantee final selection it is a mandatory clearance step for the candidates it applies to. The 22nd August 2026 sitting covered candidates applying for the following posts:

  • Police Department CAR/DAR/KSRP/IRB/KSISF Constable posts
  • Revenue Department Village Administrative Officer (VAO)
  • Land Surveyor posts (Department of Survey Settlement and Land Records)
  • Teacher posts under Karnataka Residential Education Institutions Society (KREIS)
  • Section Officer posts under the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority

  5. Match the answers against your version code and marked responses.
  6. Download and save the PDF for future reference and for use during objection filing.

KEA Kannada Language Test 2026 Objection Process

Candidates who wish to challenge any answer in the provisional key can do so through the official KEA Provisional Answer Key Objection Portal. The window is open from 22nd August 2026 until 24th August 2026, 12:00 noon, after which no objections will be accepted.

Steps to Raise an Objection

  1. Visit the objection portal login page at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/keaobjections.
  2. Log in using your Application Number/Register Number and the first 5 characters of your name.
  3. Enter your Date of Birth.
  4. Select the examination Compulsory Kannada – 2026 (22-08-2026).
  5. Enter the captcha code and log in.
  6. Select the question number and version code you want to object to.
  7. Upload supporting documents or proof in PDF format for each objection.
  8. Pay the applicable fee of Rs. 25/- per objection and submit.

Important Instructions

  • Every objection must clearly mention the question number and version code, and must be supported by valid proof in PDF format.
  • A fee of Rs. 25/- is charged per objection raised; this fee is non-refundable.
  • Objections that do not correctly mention the question number or version code, or that lack valid supporting proof, will not be considered.
  • The decision of the subject expert committee reviewing the objections will be treated as final.
  • Objections cannot be submitted after 24th August 2026, 12:00 noon.

Also Read: HTET Result 2026

What Happens After the Objection Window Closes

Once the objection window closes on 24th August 2026, the subject expert committee will review all objections submitted by candidates. Based on this review, KEA will release the final answer key for the Kannada Language Test. Results will then be prepared using the final key, feeding into the overall selection process for the respective posts Police Constable, Village Administrative Officer, Land Surveyor, KREIS Teacher, and Section Officer. The exact date for the final key and result has not been officially announced yet.

About UPSC Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination 2026

The ISS Examination is one of the premier competitive exams conducted by UPSC to recruit officers for Group A and Group B posts in the Indian Statistical Service. Understanding the exam structure helps candidates correctly interpret the provisional answer key.

The Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Examination is conducted annually by the Union Public Service Commission to fill vacancies in the Indian Statistical Service, one of India's organised Group A Central Services. The exam tests candidates on subjects including Statistics, General English, and General Studies. The Statistics papers are the most technical and weightage-heavy components of the exam. The provisional answer key released covers the objective/multiple-choice components of the Statistics papers.

ISS Examination Paper Structure

The ISS Examination 2026 Statistics papers for which the provisional answer key has been released are:

  • Statistics Paper I - Covers topics such as Probability, Statistical Methods, Numerical Analysis, and related areas.
  • Statistics Paper II - Covers topics including Linear Models, Statistical Inference, Sampling Theory, and Econometrics.

How to Raise Objections Against UPSC ISS Provisional Answer Key 2026

If a candidate disagrees with any answer published in the provisional answer key, they can submit a formal representation to UPSC within the stipulated objection window period.

UPSC allows candidates to challenge answers in the provisional answer key by submitting a formal representation. The process for raising objections is as follows:

  • Download the provisional answer key PDF for the relevant paper.
  • Identify the question number(s) where you believe the answer is incorrect.
  • Prepare a written representation with supporting references from standard textbooks or study material.
  • Submit the representation to UPSC through the official channel specified in the answer key notification (typically by post or online submission to the UPSC office).
  • UPSC will review all representations received before publishing the Final Answer Key.

What Happens After the Provisional Answer Key?

After the provisional answer key is released and the objection window closes, UPSC reviews all valid representations before publishing the Final Answer Key.

Once the objection period ends, UPSC's subject matter experts review all representations submitted by candidates. Valid objections where an answer is found to be incorrect based on credible references result in changes to the final answer key. The Final Answer Key is then published on the official website. The final marks are computed based on the final (not provisional) answer key, which forms the basis for merit list preparation and eventual selection to the Indian Statistical Service.

Sales Associate is responsible for providing the best customer experience in the stores by providing high standards of selling services to Lenskart customers. He/she plays a pivotal role in driving the revenue achieved by the store. Key responsibilities: A. Customer focus: 1. He/she must ensure the security of all Lenskart equipment and ensure there is no shortage of stock units or damage in the store. Note: This role requires working 6 days a week with a rotational week-off and rotational shifts based on business requirements. Please note that there are no night shifts. Role Snapshot
HeyBuddy (heybuddy.chat) is hiring a full-time, in-office telesales executive in Noida for freshers or candidates with up to 2 years of experience in telesales, inside sales, or lead generation. The role focuses on handling homeowner enquiries and acquiring interior designer partners, serving as the first point of contact for homeowners by responding promptly, qualifying leads, and scheduling meetings with suitable designers, while also cold-calling interior designers across Delhi NCR to onboard them as HeyBuddy partners. This is a high-volume calling role with an expectation of making 150 quality calls per day across both pipelines. There are no sales targets, revenue quotas, or closure requirements; the primary responsibility is to consistently maintain the required call volume and ensure high-quality interactions that contribute to successful conversions. Key Responsibilities: A. Homeowner enquiries: 1. Speed to lead. Call every enquiry from our website, Meta ads, and expos within minutes. The first credible call usually wins the project. 2. Qualify on the call. Location, possession status, scope, realistic budget, timeline- and disqualify politely when a lead isn't ready. A clean 'no' beats a padded pipeline. 3. Pitch with credibility, not pressure. Explain how interior projects are actually priced and executed, and why a HeyBuddy-verified designer beats a random reference. Sell by being useful, not loud. 4. Book the meeting. Your output is a confirmed designer introduction or site visit. 5. Work the follow-up cycle. Homeowners take 3–6 months to decide. Run disciplined call and WhatsApp sequences until a lead closes or dies. Most conversions happen on the fourth call, not the first. B. Designer partner acquisition: 1. Build your own list. Designers and firms across Noida, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida, and Delhi- sourced from Instagram, listings, referrals, and market research. 2. Pitch the partnership. Qualified leads, no upfront cost, pay only for introductions. Handle the repeat objections- 'we get enough leads,' 'what's your commission,' 'we tried a portal before.' 3. Screen before you sign. Qualify on portfolio, execution capability, team strength, ticket-size fit, and client feedback. Thirty good firms beat three hundred listed ones. 4. Close and onboard. Documentation, commission terms, platform onboarding- until they are live and receiving leads. C. Pipeline and loop-closing: 1. Log every dial, connect, disposition, and next action the same day. An untracked call didn't happen. 2. Nothing sits untouched beyond 72 hours. 3. Reconfirm every site visit the day before, and call after every meeting for feedback. 4. Report what homeowners and designers actually say- objections, pricing concerns, competitor mentions- straight to marketing, product, and the founders. What you're measured on: 1. Everything on this list is inside your control. 2. 150 calls a day. The one hard number. 3. Talk time. Calls ending in eleven seconds don't count for much. 4. Call quality. Reviewed from recordings- did you ask, listen, and advise honestly? 5. Follow-up adherence. Every open lead contacted on schedule. 6. CRM hygiene. Logged same day, every day. 7. Conversions, site visits, and partner activations are tracked- but they're the company's scoreboard, not a quota over your head. Who fits: 1. Fluent Hindi and working English. 2. Comfortable dialling all day- reads a room over the phone. 3. Writes a clean CRM note. 4. Prior experience in real estate, interiors, edtech, or any high-volume inside sales floor is an advantage, not a requirement.

About This Role

  • Enjoy a variety of field work and office-based work

Do you have great communication skills and want to be a role model to people hoping for a second chance? If you want to make time to help people get their lives back on track, read on.

Who are we?

Community Work and Partnerships We are responsible for the development of mutually beneficial partnerships with government agencies and non-government organisations so that individuals can undertake unpaid work as part of their community-based sentence imposed by the Courts of Victoria. Community work serves as a valuable way for individuals to pay back the community while also reconnecting and reintegrating into the community. We ensure individuals make genuine efforts to undergo rehabilitation, and we keep low risk individuals out of prison and help them contribute to the community.

What does a Field Officer do?

Your primary responsibility as a Field Officer will be to supervise a team of clients at community work sites and other community work programs. A field officer carries out many duties and functions, mainly the supervision of individuals completing community work tasks. Other responsibilities include performing site inspections, assess hazards, providing informed workplace health and safety advice, guidance and instruction; maintaining tools and equipment resister and ensuring repairs are undertaken.

A day in the life of a Field Officer. . .

Your shift starts at a Justice Service Centre location where you collect a bus/ trailer with equipment. You then drive to a site to collect a group of clients, where you will induct, instruct and transport them to a partner not-for-profit organisation in the community. Tasks for the day may involve graffiti removal, painting, litter collection, mowing and weeding. Your responsibility is to instruct the individuals to safely perform each task and monitor the work performed for the partner site before returning them to the drop off point and returning to your depot.

We are looking for individuals with various backgrounds and experience. Some desirable skills include:

  • You'll need to be able to communicate and demonstrate a range of tasks and ensure a safe environment for work teams.
  • Have a strong understanding of Occupational Health and Safety practices and their practical application.
  • Quickly build rapport in order to understand the motivations of others, identify issues and suggest courses of action appropriate to their needs.
  • Have demonstrated ability to manage conflict and strong problem-solving skills.
  • Model appropriate behaviours and attitudes to assist individuals to develop new skills and work practices.
  • Carpentry or handyman skills
  • Gardening landscaping or painting skills

Field Officers carry out a mixture of field work and office-based work, so it's important that you are able to demonstrate computer skills and written communication skills.

Transporting individuals is also a key part of the role and Field Officers will be required to drive a 12-seater bus with trailer. A full and current drivers' licence is essential for this position.

Community Work operates seven days per week and this role will be required to work on weekends. Weekend availability is required.

For More Information About The Role Please Contact

Sarah Thompson â Manager, Community Work & Partnerships on 0407 427 396 or Sarah.Thompson@justice.vic.gov.au

How To Apply

Please click the Apply button at the bottom of this advertisement. Applications should include a resume uploaded in .doc, .docx, .pdf, .txt or .rtf formats.

The Assessment Process Will Entail The Following

  • Several questions in the application form upon submitting your resume
  • A phone screen
  • An interview
  • Reference checks
  • Security checks
  • Health assessment â medical history and physical fitness components

The successful candidate will be required to undergo pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, nationally coordinated criminal history checks (NCCHC), and misconduct screening. Dependant on the role, other checks may include VicRoads checks, drivers licence checks, medical checks, Working with Children Checks, and Declaration of Private Interests (for executive and responsible officer roles).

If you require adjustments to the recruitment and selection process, or require an alternative format to any of the application material, please don't hesitate to get in touch with the contact person listed on this ad.

Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply.

Child Safe Statement Of Commitment

The Department of Justice and Community Safety is committed to the safety and wellbeing of children and young people. We seek to prevent harm of any kind impacting children and young people and have zero tolerance for racism, child abuse and inequality. Children and young people's rights, relationships, identity, and culture must be recognised and respected, their voices heard, and their concerns acted upon. We aim to foster a culturally safe, child safe and child friendly environment for all children and young people we have contact with, deliver services to, or are impacted by our work.
